description: A 4-bit barrel shifter that performs left and right shifts based on a control signal. The control signal determines the shift direction and the number of bits to shift.
code:
module barrel_shifter (
    input [3:0] data_in,
    input [1:0] shift_amount,
    input shift_dir, // 0 for left shift, 1 for right shift
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (shift_dir)
            0: // Left shift
                case (shift_amount)
                    2'b00: data_out = data_in;         // No shift
                    2'b01: data_out = data_in << 1;    // Shift left by 1
                    2'b10: data_out = data_in << 2;    // Shift left by 2
                    2'b11: data_out = data_in << 3;    // Shift left by 3
                    default: data_out = 4'b0000;
                endcase
            1: // Right shift
                case (shift_amount)
                    2'b00: data_out = data_in;         // No shift
                    2'b01: data_out = data_in >> 1;    // Shift right by 1
                    2'b10: data_out = data_in >> 2;    // Shift right by 2
                    2'b11: data_out = data_in >> 3;    // Shift right by 3
                    default: data_out = 4'b0000;
                endcase
        endcase
    end
endmodule

Design a Stop-and-Wait protocol module in Verilog. The module should include a sender and receiver state machine that operates with an acknowledgment mechanism. The sender should send a data bit and wait for an acknowledgment before sending the next bit. The data and acknowledgment signals should be controlled by clock and reset signals.
code:
module stop_and_wait(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start_send,
    input ack,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg send,
    output reg done
);
    reg [1:0] state;
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, SEND = 2'b01, WAIT_ACK = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            send <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            data_out <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start_send) begin
                        data_out <= data_out + 1; // Increment data to send
                        send <= 1;
                        state <= SEND;
                    end
                end
                SEND: begin
                    if (send) send <= 0; // Sending data
                    state <= WAIT_ACK;
                end
                WAIT_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        done <= 1; // Acknowledgment received
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end else begin
                        done <= 0; // Still waiting for acknowledgment
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module pll (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input modulated_signal,
    output reg recovered_carrier
);
    reg [3:0] phase_error;
    reg [3:0] phase;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            phase <= 0;
            recovered_carrier <= 0;
        end else begin
            phase_error <= modulated_signal ^ phase; // Simple XOR for phase error detection
            if (phase_error) begin
                phase <= phase + 1; // Adjust phase
            end
            recovered_carrier <= (phase == 4'b1111) ? 1 : 0; // Lock condition
        end
    end
endmodule

    input clk,
    input reset,
    input actual_branch,
    input [1:0] state, // Current state (2-bits)
    output reg predicted_branch,
    output reg [1:0] next_state
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            next_state <= 2'b00; // Reset to strongly not taken
            predicted_branch <= 1'b0; // Predict not taken
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // Strongly not taken
                    predicted_branch <= 1'b0;
                    next_state <= actual_branch ? 2'b01 : 2'b00; // Transition
                end
                2'b01: begin // Weakly not taken
                    predicted_branch <= 1'b0;
                    next_state <= actual_branch ? 2'b10 : 2'b00; // Transition
                end
                2'b10: begin // Weakly taken
                    predicted_branch <= 1'b1;
                    next_state <= actual_branch ? 2'b11 : 2'b01; // Transition
                end
                2'b11: begin // Strongly taken
                    predicted_branch <= 1'b1;
                    next_state <= actual_branch ? 2'b11 : 2'b10; // Transition
                end
                default: begin
                    predicted_branch <= 1'b0;
                    next_state <= 2'b00; // Default case
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire reset,      // Asynchronous reset
    input wire input_signal, // Input signal to be tracked
    output reg locked      // Output indicates if PLL is locked
);
    reg [1:0] state;      // State register

    // State encoding:
    // 00 - Unlocking
    // 01 - Locked
    // 10 - Unlocking
    // 11 - Searching

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Reset state
            locked <= 0;    // Not locked
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // Unlocking
                    if (input_signal == 1) begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Transition to Locked
                    end
                end

                2'b01: begin // Locked
                    locked <= 1; // Indicate locked
                    if (input_signal == 0) begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // Transition to Unlocking
                    end
                end

                2'b10: begin // Unlocking
                    if (input_signal == 1) begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Transition to Locked
                    end
                end

                default: state <= 2'b00; // Default to Unlocking
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a Verilog module that performs a simple Breadth-First Search (BFS) traversal on a fixed-size binary tree of depth 3. The module should take the current node index as input and output the values of the nodes in BFS order starting from the given index. The binary tree is represented as an array where for a node at index `i`, its left child is at index `2*i + 1` and its right child is at index `2*i + 2`. The module should use a clock signal to update the output on each clock cycle until all nodes are traversed.
code:
module bfs_traversal (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [2:0] start_index,
    output reg [7:0] bfs_output,
    output reg done
);
    reg [7:0] tree [0:14]; // Array to hold the binary tree values
    reg [3:0] queue [0:14]; // Queue for BFS traversal
    reg [3:0] front, rear; // Queue pointers
    reg [3:0] current_index; // Current node index
    
    initial begin
        // Initialize the binary tree values
        tree[0] = 8'd1;  // Level 0
        tree[1] = 8'd2;  // Level 1
        tree[2] = 8'd3;  // Level 1
        tree[3] = 8'd4;  // Level 2
        tree[4] = 8'd5;  // Level 2
        tree[5] = 8'd6;  // Level 2
        tree[6] = 8'd7;  // Level 2
        tree[7] = 8'd8;  // Level 3
        tree[8] = 8'd9;  // Level 3
        tree[9] = 8'd10; // Level 3
        tree[10] = 8'd11; // Level 3
        tree[11] = 8'd12; // Level 3
        tree[12] = 8'd13; // Level 3
        tree[13] = 8'd14; // Level 3
        tree[14] = 8'd15; // Level 3
    end
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            front <= 0;
            rear <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            bfs_output <= 0;
            current_index <= start_index;
        end else begin
            if (front <= rear && !done) begin
                bfs_output <= queue[front];
                front <= front + 1; // Dequeue
                
                // Enqueue left child
                if (current_index*2 + 1 < 15) begin
                    queue[rear] <= current_index*2 + 1;
                    rear <= rear + 1;
                end
                // Enqueue right child
                if (current_index*2 + 2 < 15) begin
                    queue[rear] <= current_index*2 + 2;
                    rear <= rear + 1;
                end
                current_index <= queue[front]; // Move to next index
                
                if (front > rear) begin
                    done <= 1; // BFS completed
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

);

            data_out <= 0;
            ack_sent <= 0;
            resend <= 0;

                end

module wallace_tree_adder (
    input [3:0] A,
    input [3:0] B,
    output [4:0] SUM
);
    wire [3:0] p; // Partial products
    wire [4:0] s; // Intermediate sums

    assign p = A & {4{B}}; // Generate partial products

    // First stage of reduction
    assign s[0] = p[0]; // First bit remains the same
    assign s[1] = p[1] ^ p[2]; // Sum of bit 1 and 2
    assign s[2] = (p[1] & p[2]); // Carry out for bit 1 and 2
    assign s[3] = p[3] ^ s[2]; // Sum of current bit and carry
    assign s[4] = p[3] & s[2]; // Final carry out

    // Final sum output
    assign SUM = {s[4], s[3], s[1], s[0]}; // Concatenate final outputs
endmodule

Design an 8-bit deserializer that takes a serial input bit stream and outputs the 8 bits in parallel. The deserializer should accept a clock signal and a reset signal. It should also include a valid signal that indicates when the output is valid. The input bit stream is fed in one bit at a time, and the output should be available after 8 clock cycles.

module deserializer (

    input reset,
    input serial_in,
    output reg [7:0] parallel_out,
    output reg valid
);

            parallel_out <= 0;
            valid <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (count < 8) begin
                parallel_out[count] <= serial_in; // Shift in the serial bit

                valid <= 0; // Not valid until we have 8 bits

                valid <= 1; // Set valid when we have 8 bits

Design a JK flip-flop in Verilog. The JK flip-flop should have the following inputs and outputs:

- RST (1-bit, active high reset signal)

Outputs:

- Qn (1-bit, inverted current state)

    input wire CLK,
    input wire RST,

Design a simple Stop-and-Wait protocol in Verilog. The protocol should have a sender and a receiver. The sender sends a single bit over a channel and waits for an acknowledgment (ACK) from the receiver. If the ACK is received, the sender can send the next bit. If not, it will resend the bit. The sender should have a toggle signal to indicate a new bit to send. The receiver should acknowledge the received bit with an ACK signal.

module stop_and_wait (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input send_bit,
    input ack,
    output reg send_signal,
    output reg ack_signal
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: waiting, 1: sending, 2: acked

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            send_signal <= 0;
            ack_signal <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // waiting for send
                    if (send_bit) begin
                        send_signal <= 1; // start sending
                        state <= 1;
                    end
                end
                1: begin // sending
                    if (ack) begin
                        ack_signal <= 1; // acknowledge received
                        state <= 2;
                    end else begin
                        send_signal <= 1; // resend
                    end
                end
                2: begin // acked
                    send_signal <= 0; // stop sending
                    ack_signal <= 0; // reset ACK
                    state <= 0; // go back to waiting
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input disconnect_request,

                IDLE: begin
                    if (connect_request) state <= CONNECTING;

                    state <= CONNECTED; // Automatically go to CONNECTED after CONNECTING

                DISCONNECTED: begin

        if (start) begin
            x0 <= x;
            valid <= 0; // Set valid low until calculation is done

  - `data_in`: a 32-bit data input representing the packet to be transmitted.
- Outputs:
  - `transmitting`: a signal that indicates whether a packet is currently being transmitted.
  - `data_out`: a 32-bit output representing the transmitted packet.

The transmission process activates when `start_tx` is high. The `transmitting` signal should be high during the transmission, which lasts for a fixed number of clock cycles (let's say 4 cycles). After transmission, `data_out` should hold the value of `data_in`, and `transmitting` should go low.
code:
module ethernet_mac_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start_tx,
    input wire [31:0] data_in,
    output reg transmitting,
    output reg [31:0] data_out
);
    reg [1:0] state;
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, TRANSMITTING = 2'b01, DONE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            transmitting <= 0;
            data_out <= 32'b0;
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start_tx) begin
                        transmitting <= 1;
                        data_out <= data_in;
                        state <= TRANSMITTING;
                    end
                end
                TRANSMITTING: begin
                    if (transmitting) begin
                        state <= DONE; // move to done state after 4 cycles
                    end
                end
                DONE: begin
                    transmitting <= 0;
                    state <= IDLE; // go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

The state transitions should occur based on the input signals: start (to begin initialization) and ready (indicating the PCIe is ready for data transfer). After the data transfer is complete, the state should transition to DONE.
code:
module pcie_fsm (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire ready,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: INIT, 10: DATA_TRANSFER, 11: DONE
);

    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE = 2'b00,
               INIT = 2'b01,
               DATA_TRANSFER = 2'b10,
               DONE = 2'b11;

    // Sequential logic: State transition
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start)
                        state <= INIT;
                end
                INIT: begin
                    state <= DATA_TRANSFER; // Transition to DATA_TRANSFER after INIT
                end
                DATA_TRANSFER: begin
                    if (ready)
                        state <= DONE; // Transition to DONE when ready
                end
                DONE: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Transition back to IDLE after DONE
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module bluetooth_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start_connect,
    input connection_success,
    output reg [1:0] state // 2 bits for 3 states (00: IDLE, 01: CONNECTING, 10: CONNECTED)
);

    localparam IDLE = 2'b00;
    localparam CONNECTING = 2'b01;
    localparam CONNECTED = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start_connect) begin
                        state <= CONNECTING;
                    end
                end
                CONNECTING: begin
                    if (connection_success) begin
                        state <= CONNECTED;
                    end
                end
                CONNECTED: begin
                    if (reset) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // Goes to IDLE if reset is asserted
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
